sites.name: Tower Bridge
sites.fact: Opened in 1894. The roadway splits into two bascules that lift to let tall ships through, around 800 times a year.
sites.hint: The bridge with two stone towers, just east of the Tower of London.

sites.name: Big Ben
sites.fact: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell, not the tower. The tower itself was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
sites.hint: The clock tower at the north end of the Houses of Parliament, beside Westminster Bridge.

sites.name: London Eye
sites.fact: A 135-metre observation wheel opened in 2000. One turn takes about half an hour.
sites.hint: The big wheel on the south bank, across the river from Westminster.

sites.name: St Paul's Cathedral
sites.fact: Christopher Wren's cathedral was completed in 1710, after the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed the one before it. Its dome is 111 metres high.
sites.hint: The great dome in the City, north of the Millennium Bridge.

sites.name: The Shard
sites.fact: At 310 metres, the tallest building in the United Kingdom. It was completed in 2012.
sites.hint: The glass spike beside London Bridge station, south of the river.

sites.name: Buckingham Palace
sites.fact: The monarch's London home since 1837. It has 775 rooms.
sites.hint: At the end of the Mall, between Green Park and St James's Park.

sites.name: Tower of London
sites.fact: William the Conqueror began the White Tower in the 1070s. The Crown Jewels are kept here.
sites.hint: The castle on the north bank beside Tower Bridge.

sites.name: Hyde Park
sites.fact: 350 acres, open to the public since 1637. The Serpentine lake was made in the 1730s.
sites.hint: The large park west of Mayfair, with a long curved lake.

sites.name: Canary Wharf
sites.fact: A financial district built on the old West India Docks from the late 1980s. One Canada Square was Britain's tallest building until the Shard.
sites.hint: The cluster of towers inside the big loop of the river to the east.

sites.name: Royal Observatory
sites.fact: The prime meridian, zero degrees longitude, runs through this hilltop observatory, founded in 1675.
sites.hint: On the hill in Greenwich Park, south of the river bend.

sites.name: Wembley Stadium
sites.fact: England's national football stadium, rebuilt and reopened in 2007. Its arch is 133 metres high.
sites.hint: Look for the white arch, far to the north-west.

sites.name: Battersea Power Station
sites.fact: A coal-fired power station with four chimneys, built between 1929 and 1955. After decades empty it reopened in 2022 with shops, offices and homes.
sites.hint: Four white chimneys on the south bank, upstream of Westminster.
